that drives the experiment gate (`GET /api/experiments/{id}/gate`) so a pipeline can block a deploy on an eval regression: ```bash pip install ./cli # or: PYTHONPATH=cli/src python -m REDACTED_cli … REDACTED gate \ --url https://your-REDACTED-api.example.com \ --workflow \ --dataset \ --threshold 0.5 # max allowed drop in avg eval vs baseline ``` The command creates a `kind=regression` experiment (candidate = latest version, baseline = previous; override with `--version`/`--baseline`), polls the gate, prints the verdict, and exits `0` on pass, `1` on regression, `2` on error/`not_applicable`. Auth: `--key` or `$AEGIS_API_KEY`, sent as `X-Aegis-API-Key` (only needed when the server has `AUTH_ENABLE…226 tokens truncated…le guardrail judge credentials - [ ] `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` set before issuing webhook signing secrets or storing MCP/integration credentials - [ ] `CORS_ORIGINS` locked to your UI origin - [ ] Tracing / LangSmith / webhooks configured if you need them --- ### Published invocation credentials and hosted chat Publish a version, then open **More actions → Deploy details** to issue a scoped invoke key, webhook signing secret, or chat token. Credentials appear once; store them server-side. Repeated issuance rotates the value; revoke removes access. Publishing another version revokes all issued deployment credentials. Existing publications require provisioning after migration. Invoke keys are hashed; webhook secrets are Fernet-encrypted. Account `X-Aegis-API-Key` authenticates management only, not invocation. For signed webhooks, concatenate UTF-8 `POST\n{request_path}\n{deployment_id}\n{version_id}\n{timestamp}\n{nonce}\n` with the **exact raw request body**. Set `X-Aegis-Signature` to `sha256=` followed by the hex HMAC-SHA256 digest using the deployment secret. Send `X-Aegis-Timestamp` as Unix seconds (within ±300 seconds) and `X-Aegis-Nonce` as a fresh URL-safe 16–128-character value. Reused nonces return HTTP 409. Hosted chat (`/chat/[deploymentId]`) exchanges a scoped chat token for an HTTP-only session cookie (`/v1/chat/session`), bound to the deployment. The chat UI can run standalone or in an iframe with cookie fallback, calling `/v1/chat/invoke` to interact with the pinned workflow version. --- ### Durable execution, restarts, and database-backed approvals Aegis implements durable execution with database-backed checkpoints and human approvals across process restarts and separate API/worker nodes. 1. **Checkpoints & Restart Recovery:** Every node execution records a row in `run_checkpoints` (`started` upon entry, `completed` with node output alongside `NodeResult`, or `skipped` for conditional branches). Checkpoints snapshot context state and pending memory writes. On application boot or worker recovery (`recover_stale_runs`), orphaned runs are re-queued. `compute_resume` identifies the uncompleted execution frontier and pins outputs from completed checkpoints. Graph execution rewires triggers into the frontier, restoring context and avoiding redundant node re-execution. 2. **Database-Backed Approval Gates & Notifications:** Human Approval nodes and pre-execution tool review gates persist their wait state in the `approval_requests` database table. - Wait state records assignee, positive escalation timeout, parked/approved/denied/timed_out status, resolution timestamps, and sanitized delivery diagnostics. - Parking dispatches `approval_requested` to the workflow webhook and bound Slack/email credentials (email requires SMTP configuration; delivery errors are recorded safely and never approve runs). - If the gate remains pending when `escalationTimeoutSeconds` elapses, a single `approval_escalated` reminder is sent without granting approval. - `wait_for_approval` anchors deadlines to `parked_at` (wall clock) and polls the database row every second, augmented by Postgres `LISTEN`/`NOTIFY` wake-ups. - Approvals are **durable across server restarts and worker/API separation**: decisions submitted to the API resolve waits executing in worker processes via atomic row compare-and-swap (CAS). If a server restarts while a run is waiting, the interrupted approval row is marked `cancelled` and the recovered run re-parks the node with a fresh approval request row. - `POST /api/runs/{id}/approve` requires `{ "approval_id": "", "approved": true, "comment": "..." }`. Stale or mismatched IDs return HTTP 409 and cannot approve subsequent calls. 3. **Durability vs. Exactly-Once Guarantees:** Database-backed durability guarantees that orchestrator state, approval records, and completed checkpoint outputs survive process restarts without losing workflow progress. However, **this is distinct from distributed exactly-once execution guarantees for external side effects**. If a node performs an external action (such as dispatching an un-idempotent HTTP request or publishing a message) and the system crashes before checkpoint commit, resumption executes from the frontier. Nodes with external side effects should be idempotent or use downstream deduplication keys. --- ### Knowledge Base & RAG Aegis includes built-in RAG capabilities for document indexing and grounded retrieval: - **Document Ingestion:** Upload PDF, DOCX, Markdown, or plain text documents in the workflow data panel. Files are chunked using sentence-aware boundary detection (800 characters, 120 character overlap) and tracked with source provenance and metadata. - **Knowledge libraries:** User-owned libraries on the `/knowledge` page, separate from per-workflow documents. Ingest by pasting text, uploading a file (PDF, DOCX, MD, TXT up to 8 MB), or fetching a public URL. Chunk strategy (sentence, paragraph, or fixed; 200–4000 chars, overlap below size) applies on the next ingest; reindex refreshes embeddings only. Up to 12 lowercase tags per library AND-filter queries, and ingest enforces a 5000-chunk cap. - **Retrieval methods:** keyword, BM25, TF-IDF, embedding, and hybrid (reciprocal rank fusion, candidate pool up to 200, default 60), with optional LLM rerank (pool of 1–50) and query rewrite — both degrade to the original order with a recorded note when no model key exists or the call fails. The minimum-score filter applies before reranking so a ranker cannot promote hits back over the threshold. A query bench tries unsaved settings before committing them. - **Pluggable Vector Stores:** Configured via `VECTOR_STORE=auto|pgvector|sqlite_vec|none`. On PostgreSQL, `auto` uses `pgvector` with cosine distance indexes (`vector(768)`). On SQLite, `auto` utilizes `sqlite-vec` for native local KNN vector queries, falling back to JSON similarity search when extensions are unavailable. - **Retrieval Nodes:** `kb_retrieve` nodes query indexed collections with top-k ranking, relevance thresholds, and formatted citation output for downstream LLM synthesis — optionally pinned to a source library with a method override. --- ### Agent structured output, loops & trace insights - **Structured output:** Agent nodes accept an `outputSchema` (scalar fields, scalar arrays, one nested object, up to 32 properties) enforced at run time with one repair pass; the output-schema clause stays out of the prompt unless a schema is set. - **Loop node:** Repeats a template or sub-workflow while a condition holds, up to `maxIterations` (1–25) so the graph stays acyclic. `{{iteration}}` is 1-based and `{{last_output}}` carries the previous body result, including dotted `{{last_output.field}}` paths into JSON bodies. The per-item `iteration` node (over `{{item}}` / `{{index}}`) remains for list fan-out. - **Trace insights:** Observability → Review groups completed runs that share an output pattern when an eval score is low (1–5 judge scores normalized) or a thumbs-down was left, with at least 2 occurrences. Insights queue directly into the annotation queue for labeling. --- ### Agent tool loops and MCP (client and server) Agent nodes can select builtin Tool declarations or discovered tools from Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. - **MCP Client for Agents:** Agent nodes attach discovered tools from named MCP servers registered in **Settings → MCP servers**. Transports support `stdio` (launches local commands via argv without a shell, gated by `MCP_STDIO_ENABLED=true`) and `streamable_http` (HTTP endpoints with DNS pinning and private network host allowlists). Credentials are encrypted at rest with `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY`. Tool schemas enforce bounded linear regex validation to protect against catastrophic backtracking. - **Agent Configuration & Execution Budget:** Agent nodes configure attached tools, iteration limits, and cumulative token budgets: ```json { "tools": [ { "kind": "node", "nodeId": "calculator", "requireApproval": true }, { "kind": "mcp", "credentialId": "", "toolName": "add" } ], "maxToolIterations": 8, "tokenBudget": 8192 } ``` `maxToolIterations` (default 8) bounds model tool-call response cycles. `tokenBudget` (default 8192) tracks cumulative prompt, completion, and thinking tokens across iterations and search calls. Breaching either budget cleanly halts tool dispatch and follows configured node error branches. Tools with `requireApproval: true` serialize review through the database-backed approval gate prior to invocation. - **Published Workflow MCP Server:** Aegis serves as an MCP server at `/mcp` and `/mcp/` using stateless Streamable HTTP. Published workflows are dynamically exposed as executable MCP tools. Requests authenticate via deployment credentials (`X-Aegis-Deployment-ID`, `X-Aegis-Version-ID`, and `X-Aegis-Invoke-Key` or HMAC signature) and execute through `invoke_and_wait`. --- ### Datasets, experiments, and annotation queue - **Dataset CSV Import:** Experiments accepts CSV columns `input`, optional `expected_output`, and optional `metadata` (JSON object). Quoted/multiline CSV is supported; invalid rows reject the entire batch with row errors. - **Feedback & Annotation Queue:** Thumbs-down ratings from users or operators enqueue runs into the annotation queue (`/observability`). Reviewers can inspect inputs, outputs, and execution traces, apply corrected gold labels, and promote them directly into evaluation datasets. - **Cluster & Run Promotion:** Runs and failure cluster samples can be copied into target datasets, deduplicated by `source_run` with provenance preserved. - **Provider Pricing:** Cost tracking uses an offline LiteLLM catalog with provider-scoped aliases. Unpriced or subscription models display `—` instead of false zero totals. --- ### Observability, Tracing, and LangSmith Aegis provides deep operational visibility for production agent workflows: - **OpenTelemetry (OTLP):** Export standard spans for workflow runs, node executions, and LLM calls to Jaeger, Langfuse, or any OTLP collector. - **LangSmith Tracing:** Export every run and model call directly to LangSmith over OTLP (`LANGSMITH_ENABLED=true`). - **Privacy & Sanitization by Default:** Prompts, outputs, tool arguments, retrieved chunks, and error texts are stripped unless explicitly enabled via `LANGSMITH_CAPTURE_CONTENT=true`. Passwords, API keys, and bearer tokens are deeply redacted across nested JSON structures. - **Attempt Tracking:** Each run attempt is exported as a detached `workflow.run` root linked to the parent request context. Execution attempts across checkpoint resumes are tracked in `metrics_json.trace_attempts` and displayed in the UI badge. - **Graceful Worker Drain:** Both API and worker processes drain active executions and await span finalization before shutting down tracer providers. - **Triage & Feedback Loops:** Observability surfaces include live SSE run streaming, failure cluster grouping, cross-run trace search (`/api/observability/spans`), and cost breakdowns per node and model. --- ## Contributing 1. # Aegis frontend Next.js 14 (App Router) workbench for the Aegis backend: the React Flow canvas, run/observability surfaces, prompts, playground, knowledge libraries, and hosted chat — plus the public `/welcome` landing page. ## Develop ```bash cp .env.local.example .env.local # set NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:8000 npm install npm run dev # http://localhost:3000 ``` Requires the backend running (`../backend`, default `http://127.0.0.1:8000`). ## Gate ```bash npm run typecheck # tsc --noEmit npm run lint # next lint npm run build ``` All backend calls go through `src/lib/api.ts`; TanStack Query cache keys live in `src/lib/query-keys.ts`; SSE proxies under `src/app/api/*/stream/route.ts`. --- docs architecture --- # Aegis — System Architecture Aegis is a visual agent-workflow workbench: users compose graph workflows (LLM agents, tools, routers, guardrails, evals) on a React Flow canvas, run them against real inputs via Google ADK (Gemini natively; OpenAI, Anthropic, and other providers through LiteLLM), and operate them through an observability/triage surface. Two apps live in one repo: `backend/` (FastAPI, Python 3.12) and `frontend/` (Next.js 14 App Router, TypeScript). The diagrams below are Mermaid and render directly on GitHub. ## 1. System overview The frontend never talks to an LLM provider and never touches the database — every call goes through the typed client (`frontend/src/lib/api.ts`) to the FastAPI backend. Server-sent events (run stream, observability stream) are proxied through Next.js route handlers under `src/app/api/*/stream/` rather than hitting the backend directly. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph browser["Browser"] UI["Next.js 14 App Router UI
React Flow canvas · TanStack Query
frontend/src"] end subgraph nextsrv["Next.js server"] PROXY["SSE proxy route handlers
src/app/api/*/stream"] end subgraph fastapi["FastAPI backend (port 8000)"] MW["Middleware: CORS · optional X-Aegis-API-Key auth
viewer role · rate limits"] ROUTERS["Routers — app/api/*"] SVC["Services — app/services/* (~60 modules)"] EXEC["Executor + durable run_events log
+ local _RunEventBroker fan-out"] end DB[("Postgres (prod) / SQLite (dev, tests)
schema owned by Alembic")] ADK["Google ADK Runner"] LLM["LLM providers — Gemini native,
others via LiteLLM"] UI -->|"typed client — src/lib/api.ts"| MW UI -->|"EventSource"| PROXY -->|"SSE"| MW MW --> ROUTERS --> SVC --> DB SVC --> EXEC --> ADK --> LLM ``` ## 2. Run pipeline (the core loop) Workflow graphs are stored as JSON (`nodes` + `edges`). A run passes through three services in order: **validation** (`graph_validation.py`, must be Trigger → … → End, acyclic, no orphan edges), **compilation** (`compiler.py`, graph JSON → ADK `Workflow`; non-LLM node behaviors come from `_make_*_fn` factories in `node_handlers.py`), and **execution** (`executor.py`, persists each emitted event to `run_events` with a per-run seq, fans out to SSE subscribers through the local `_RunEventBroker`, and wakes remote processes via Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY; applies guardrail policies and eval thresholds, and records observability rollups). Phase 1 agent nodes use `agent_tools.py`: a native ADK `Agent(tools=[FunctionTool, ...])` runs inside a canvas-node wrapper. References point to disconnected builtin Tool declarations or owned/discovered MCP credential tools; declarations remain in stored canvas JSON but are excluded from the executable DAG. The wrapper renders instructions at execution, enforces `maxToolIterations`/`tokenBudget`, preserves node error branches, and stops whole-node retries once tool execution starts. Each invocation becomes a distinct child `RunSpan`, including parallel repeated calls and failures/cancellation. Token usage covers nested grounded Google Search and fails closed when accounting is unavailable. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber participant UI as Frontend participant API as app/api/runs.py participant VAL as graph_validation.py participant CMP as compiler.py participant EXE as executor.py participant ADK as ADK Runner + LLM provider participant DB as Database UI->>API: POST run (workflow, input) API->>VAL: validate DAG (Trigger → … → End, acyclic) API->>DB: create WorkflowRun API->>EXE: schedule (inline) / worker claims (worker mode) EXE->>CMP: compile_workflow(graph JSON) CMP-->>EXE: ADK Workflow (agents, join nodes, routed edges) EXE->>ADK: execute via Runner ADK-->>EXE: node events (streamed) EXE-->>UI: SSE via _RunEventBroker (through Next proxy) EXE->>EXE: apply guardrail policies + eval thresholds EXE->>DB: NodeResult · LlmCall · RunSpan · observability rollups ``` ## 3. Backend layering Strict layering: routers parse and authorize, schemas shape the payloads, services hold all business logic, and a single SQLAlchemy models file talks to the database. All settings live in `app/config.py` (`Settings`) — env vars are never read directly. The app deliberately does **not** call `Base.metadata.create_all()` on startup; `app/services/startup.py` gates boot on the database being at Alembic head. ```mermaid flowchart TB MW["app/main.py — FastAPI app
CORS · optional API-key auth + viewer role · rate limits · lifespan"] R["app/api — 16 routers, one per resource
workflows · runs · observability · credentials · guardrail_policies
datasets · experiments · feedback · alerts · templates · jobs
eval_presets · node_test · assist · meta · platform"] S["app/schemas — Pydantic request/response models"] SVC["app/services — all business logic (~60 modules)
graph_validation · compiler · node_handlers · executor
llm_providers · guardrail* · eval* · observability_* · knowledge_*
credentials (Fernet) · run_worker · schedule_worker · job_queue · tracing"] M["app/db/models.py — single SQLAlchemy models file"] DB[("Postgres / SQLite")] AL["alembic/ — owns the schema
startup gate: DB must be at head"] CFG["app/config.py — Settings
(only place env is read)"] MW --> R --> S --> SVC --> M --> DB AL -.->|"migrations"| DB CFG -.-> MW CFG -.-> SVC ``` ## 4. Node type system (spans both apps) Adding or changing a node type touches a fixed set of files that must stay in sync across the two apps. The backend registry (`node_registry.py`) is canonical and is served to the UI. ```mermaid flowchart LR NT(["A node type
(e.g. agent, guardrail, router)"]) subgraph BE["Backend — backend/app/services"] REG["node_registry.py
canonical metadata, served to the UI"] NH["node_handlers.py
_make_*_fn execution factory"] CP["compiler.py
wiring into the ADK Workflow"] GV["graph_validation.py
structural rules (if any)"] end subgraph FE["Frontend — frontend/src"] TW["types/workflow.ts
NodeType union + node data types"] NR["lib/node-registry.ts
labels · icons · categories"] CN["components/canvas/nodes/*
canvas renderer component"] end NT --> REG NT --> NH NT --> CP NT --> GV NT --> TW NT --> NR NT --> CN ``` The registry currently defines 31 node types across six categories: | Category | Node types | |---|---| | `flow` (13) | trigger, end, input_schema, if, switch, filter, human_approval, sub_workflow, router, classifier, join, iteration, loop | | `data` (8) | transform, set_fields, code, memory_store, memory_retrieve, kb_retrieve, json_parse, delay | | `llm` (4) | agent, summarizer, translator, extractor | | `tools` (2) | tool, integration | | `quality` (2) | evaluation, guardrail | | `annotate` (2) | note, group (neither is executable) | `frontend/src/types/workflow.ts` mirrors all 31 in its `NodeType` union. The palette in `frontend/src/lib/node-registry.ts` intentionally defines only 30 — `group` is a display-only frame created from the canvas toolbar, not dragged in from the palette. `loop` repeats a template or sub-workflow while a condition holds (capped by `maxIterations`, 1–25) with `{{iteration}}` and `{{last_output}}` in scope; agent nodes separately accept an `outputSchema` enforced with one repair pass. ## 5. LLM provider layer Every LLM call routes through `app/services/llm_providers/` — the single seam between graph nodes and model APIs. `registry.py` holds the static provider catalog; `llm_providers/__init__.py` resolves a node's `provider` / `model` / `credentialId` / `credentialName` (plus the run's `_user_id`) into a `ProviderModel` and dispatches it. | Provider id | Label | Invocation path | Key source | |---|---|---|---| | `google` | Google Gemini | native `google-genai` (default) | `GOOGLE_API_KEY` env only | | `openai` | OpenAI | LiteLLM | credential or `OPENAI_API_KEY` | | `anthropic` | Anthropic | LiteLLM | credential or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | | `fireworks` | Fireworks AI | LiteLLM | credential or `FIREWORKS_AI_API_KEY` | | `openrouter` | OpenRouter | LiteLLM (`openrouter/…`) | credential or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | | `featherless` | Featherless AI | LiteLLM (OpenAI-compatible `api_base`) | credential or `FEATHERLESS_API_KEY` | | `vercel` | Vercel AI Gateway | LiteLLM (OpenAI-compatible `api_base`) | credential or `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` | | `ollama` | Ollama (local) | LiteLLM (OpenAI-compatible `api_base`) | keyless; `apiBase` → `OLLAMA_API_BASE` → `http://localhost:11434` | - `build_adk_model()` returns a bare model string for Gemini and wraps every other provider in ADK's `LiteLlm`, so the `Runner` is unchanged. - `generate_text()` / `generate_structured()` serve direct one-shot paths (router/classifier decisions, guardrail LLM checks, deferred evals, and no-tools node previews): Gemini natively, others via `litellm.completion` with a `json_object` retry when a provider rejects `json_schema`. - Tool-enabled agents and their previews use native ADK loops, not the direct one-shot path. `maxToolIterations` defaults to 8 tool-call response batches and `tokenBudget` to 8192 reported prompt/completion/thinking tokens. Model results that breach a bound cannot invoke further tools. - Key resolution is per node: a bound credential (Fernet-encrypted, per-user) wins over the provider's env var. Google is env-only; every other provider id is also a credential `type`. - `GET /api/meta/models` exposes the catalog with per-provider `configured` flags, and `workflow_capabilities.py` gates run creation on the provider keys a graph actually needs instead of always requiring `GOOGLE_API_KEY`. - An unset or unknown provider falls back to `GEMINI_MODEL`, so existing graphs are unaffected. Adding a provider mirrors the node-type workflow: extend `registry.py` (backend, canonical), the credential types in `app/schemas/credential.py` if it takes a bound key, and `frontend/src/lib/llm-providers.ts` (UI catalog kept in sync by hand). ### MCP client boundary `mcp_client.py` uses the compatible MCP Python SDK v1 for stdio and Streamable HTTP. A named `mcp` credential stores transport configuration; migration `019_mcp_tool_cache` adds bounded public tool descriptors and discovery timestamp on that credential. Settings and the inspector use owner-scoped discovery APIs. Runtime binds the same owner ID, refreshes live schemas, and scopes initialized sessions/subprocesses to the agent node with deterministic cancellation cleanup. No live sessions are cached globally. Stdio is explicit administrator opt-in (`MCP_STDIO_ENABLED`), executes argv without a shell, and inherits only minimal SDK environment plus configured values. HTTP requests revalidate/pin DNS, permit private hosts only through exact `MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, and reject redirects/compression. Nested headers/env are encrypted and masked; remote schemas cannot fetch external references and regexes use the bounded linear subset documented in README. This is a client, not an MCP endpoint for published workflows. ## 6. Execution modes and cross-process transport `RUN_EXECUTION_MODE=inline` (default) executes runs inside the API process. In `worker` mode a separate `worker.py` process claims and executes runs — the API must not also start the run worker (split-brain double-claim). Run streams and approval waits are durable, so in worker mode the API can serve `/stream` and `/approve` for runs the worker is executing: events replay from `run_events` plus cross-process NOTIFY delivery into the API's broker, and approval decisions are the `approval_requests` row (waiters poll the row every second; NOTIFY is a wake-up hint). The schedule worker (cron-style triggers) runs in the API lifespan in both modes. Human Approval nodes record the wait itself in `approval_requests`: assignee, escalation timeout, parked/approved/denied/timed_out status, resolution timestamps, and sanitized delivery failures. The row is the durable wait truth — `wait_for_approval` anchors terminal and escalation deadlines to `parked_at` (wall clock) and polls the row every second, so a decision committed by any process resolves a waiter elsewhere, and a restart re-parks the node with a fresh row (deadlines restart; the interrupted row is resolved `cancelled`). Cancellation records `cancelled`. On park, the workflow's configured `webhook_url` receives `approval_requested`; optional `approvalNotifications` bind Slack/email credentials by id/name, never copied integration secrets. Email requires an SMTP-configured credential (missing SMTP is a delivery failure, not a queued send). `approvalAssignee` names the reviewer/team. Optional positive-integer `escalationTimeoutSeconds` sends a single `approval_escalated` reminder while still parked; it never grants approval. The terminal deadline remains `APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`. Both deadlines start at park; requested delivery completes before escalation delivery, so a slow bounded transport can delay the reminder. Notifications cannot grant approval, and failures do not bypass the terminal timeout. Tool references can require approval before dispatch. Human/tool reviews share one run-wide serialized gate, so parallel nodes do not overwrite the only pending review; queued/parked time does not consume the node's active timeout. Every call has its own approval UUID and argument review. `POST /api/runs/{id}/approve` requires `{ "approval_id": "", "approved": true, "comment": "..." }`. Atomic identity/parked-state checks reject stale or mismatched decisions with HTTP 409 instead of authorizing the next call. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph inline["RUN_EXECUTION_MODE=inline (default)"] API1["API process
create_run schedules directly"] --> EX1["executor (same process)"] EX1 --> BR1["run_events log + local _RunEventBroker
LISTEN/NOTIFY fans out to API subscribers"] end subgraph workermode["RUN_EXECUTION_MODE=worker"] API2["API process
must NOT start the run worker"] -->|"writes pending run"| DB2[("Database")] W["worker.py process"] -->|"claims + executes"| DB2 W --> EX2["executor (worker process)
publishes run_events + approval rows"] API2 -->|"serves /stream via replay + NOTIFY
and /approve via row CAS"| DB2 end ``` **Durable runs (resume on restart).** Each node execution upserts a `run_checkpoints` row (`started` on `node_started`, `completed` + output in the same transaction as the `NodeResult`, `skipped` for authored pins). On boot, `recover_stale_runs` re-queues orphaned `running`/`awaiting_approval` rows (cancelling parked approval requests so the node re-parks) while `pending`/`queued` rows stay claimable; `resume_runs_on_boot`/`resume_max_attempts` gate resume vs. the old fail-all behavior. `compute_resume` derives pinned outputs and the frontier --- env example --- # Google Gemini (required) GOOGLE_API_KEY=your_google_api_key # If Gemini calls fail with "Connection refused", unset GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL in your shell # Database — SQLite for fast local dev (default); Neon for shared/staging DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///./aegis.db # DATABASE_URL=REDACTED # Optional alternative LLM providers (per-node model selection on the canvas). # When a key is set, that provider's models appear in the node model picker and # satisfy run gating. DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT=development # Auth (optional — disabled by default for local dev) AUTH_ENABLED=false # Editor key used only when AUTH_ENABLED=true. Leave empty until you generate # a real secret. The old example value "your-secret-api-key" is rejected and # will not authenticate. AEGIS_API_KEY= # Credential secret encryption at rest (Fernet). OpenAI, Anthropic, and other providers through LiteLLM), and operate them through an observability/triage surface. System overview The frontend never talks to an LLM provider and never touches the database — every call goes through the typed client (`frontend/src/lib/api.ts`) to the FastAPI backend. Server-sent events (run stream, observability stream) are proxied through Next.js route handlers under `src/app/api/*/stream/` rather than hitting the backend directly. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph browser["Browser"] UI["Next.js 14 App Router UI

Run pipeline (the core loop) Workflow graphs are stored as JSON (`nodes` + `edges`). A run passes through three services in order: **validation** (`graph_validation.py`, must be Trigger → … → End, acyclic, no orphan edges), **compilation** (`compiler.py`, graph JSON → ADK `Workflow`; non-LLM node behaviors come from `_make_*_fn` factories in `node_handlers.py`), and **execution** (`executor.py`, persists each emitted event to `run_events` with a per-run seq, fans out to SSE subscribers through the local `_RunEventBroker`, and wakes remote processes via Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY; applies guardrail policies and eval thresholds, and records observability rollups). Phase 1 agent nodes use `agent_tools.py`: a native ADK `Agent(tools=[FunctionTool, ...])` runs inside a canvas-node wrapper. References point to disconnected builtin Tool declarations or owned/discovered MCP credential tools; declarations remain in stored canvas JSON but are excluded from the executable DAG. The wrapper renders instructions at execution, enforces `maxToolIterations`/`tokenBudget`, preserves node error branches, and stops whole-node retries once tool execution starts. Each invocation becomes a distinct child `RunSpan`, including parallel repeated calls and failures/cancellation. LLM provider layer Every LLM call routes through `app/services/llm_providers/` — the single seam between graph nodes and model APIs. `registry.py` holds the static provider catalog; `llm_providers/__init__.py` resolves a node's `provider` / `model` / `credentialId` / `credentialName` (plus the run's `_user_id`) into a `ProviderModel` and dispatches it. | Provider id | Label | Invocation path | Key source | |---|---|---|---| | `google` | Google Gemini | native `google-genai` (default) | `GOOGLE_API_KEY` env only | | `openai` | OpenAI | LiteLLM | credential or `OPENAI_API_KEY` | | `anthropic` | Anthropic | LiteLLM | credential or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | | `fireworks` | Fireworks AI | LiteLLM | credential or `FIREWORKS_AI_API_KEY` | | `openrouter` | OpenRouter | LiteLLM (`openrouter/…`) | credential or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | | `featherless` | Featherless AI | LiteLLM (OpenAI-compatible `api_base`) | credential or `FEATHERLESS_API_KEY` | | `vercel` | Vercel AI Gateway | LiteLLM (OpenAI-compatible `api_base`) | credential or `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` | | `ollama` | Ollama (local) | LiteLLM (OpenAI-compatible `api_base`) | keyless; `apiBase` → `OLLAMA_API_BASE` → `http://localhost:11434` | - `build_adk_model()` returns a bare model string for Gemini and wraps every other provider in ADK's `LiteLlm`, so the `Runner` is unchanged. - `generate_text()` / `generate_structured()` serve direct one-shot paths (router/classifier decisions, guardrail LLM checks, deferred evals, and no-tools node previews): Gemini natively, others via `litellm.completion` with a `json_object` retry when a provider rejects `json_schema`. - Tool-enabled agents and their previews use native ADK loops, not the direct one-shot path. `maxToolIterations` defaults to 8 tool-call response batches and `tokenBudget` to 8192 reported prompt/completion/thinking tokens. Model results that breach a bound cannot invoke further tools. - Key resolution is per node: a bound credential (Fernet-encrypted, per-user) wins over the provider's env var. Google is env-only; every other provider id is also a credential `type`. - `GET /api/meta/models` exposes the catalog with per-provider `configured` flags, and `workflow_capabilities.py` gates run creation on the provider keys a graph actually needs instead of always requiring `GOOGLE_API_KEY`. - An unset or unknown provider falls back to `GEMINI_MODEL`, so existing graphs are unaffected. Adding a provider mirrors the node-type workflow: extend `registry.py` (backend, canonical), the credential types in `app/schemas/credential.py` if it takes a bound key, and `frontend/src/lib/llm-providers.ts` (UI catalog kept in sync by hand). ### MCP client boundary `mcp_client.py` uses the compatible MCP Python SDK v1 for stdio and Streamable HTTP. A named `mcp` credential stores transport configuration; migration `019_mcp_tool_cache` adds bounded public tool descriptors and discovery timestamp on that credential. Settings and the inspector use owner-scoped discovery APIs. Runtime binds the same owner ID, refreshes live schemas, and scopes initialized sessions/subprocesses to the agent node with deterministic cancellation cleanup. No live sessions are cached globally. Stdio is explicit administrator opt-in (`MCP_STDIO_ENABLED`), executes argv without a shell, and inherits only minimal SDK environment plus configured values. HTTP requests revalidate/pin DNS, permit private hosts only through exact `MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, and reject redirects/compression. Nested headers/env are encrypted and masked; remote schemas cannot fetch external references and regexes use the bounded linear subset documented in README. This is a client, not an MCP endpoint for published workflows. ## 6. Execution modes and cross-process transport `RUN_EXECUTION_MODE=inline` (default) executes runs inside the API process. In `worker` mode a separate `worker.py` process claims and executes runs — the API must not also start the run worker (split-brain double-claim). Run streams and approval waits are durable, so in worker mode the API can serve `/stream` and `/approve` for runs the worker is executing: events replay from `run_events` plus cross-process NOTIFY delivery into the API's broker, and approval decisions are the `approval_requests` row (waiters poll the row every second; NOTIFY is a wake-up hint). The schedule worker (cron-style triggers) runs in the API lifespan in both modes. Human Approval nodes record the wait itself in `approval_requests`: assignee, escalation timeout, parked/approved/denied/timed_out status, resolution timestamps, and sanitized delivery failures. The row is the durable wait truth — `wait_for_approval` anchors terminal and escalation deadlines to `parked_at` (wall clock) and polls the row every second, so a decision committed by any process resolves a waiter elsewhere, and a restart re-parks the node with a fresh row (deadlines restart; the interrupted row is resolved `cancelled`). Cancellation records `cancelled`. On park, the workflow's configured `webhook_url` receives `approval_requested`; optional `approvalNotifications` bind Slack/email credentials by id/name, never copied integration secrets. Email requires an SMTP-configured credential (missing SMTP is a delivery failure, not a queued send). `approvalAssignee` names the reviewer/team. Optional positive-integer `escalationTimeoutSeconds` sends a single `approval_escalated` reminder while still parked; it never grants approval. The terminal deadline remains `APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`. Both deadlines start at park; requested delivery completes before escalation delivery, so a slow bounded transport can delay the reminder. Notifications cannot grant approval, and failures do not bypass the terminal timeout. Tool references can require approval before dispatch. Human/tool reviews share one run-wide serialized gate, so parallel nodes do not overwrite the only pending review; queued/parked time does not consume the node's active timeout. Every call has its own approval UUID and argument review. `POST /api/runs/{id}/approve` requires `{ "approval_id": "", "approved": true, "comment": "..." }`. @asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    from app.services.async_tasks import set_main_loop

    init_tracing()
    # NOTE: schema is owned by Alembic (single source of truth). We intentionally
    # do NOT call Base.metadata.create_all here — run_startup_tasks() instead
    # gates boot on migrations being current (see services/startup.py).
    startup_status = run_startup_tasks()
    app.state.startup_status = startup_status
    set_main_loop(asyncio.get_running_loop())
    await startup_http_client()
    start_schedule_worker()
    # Durable event transport: LISTEN/NOTIFY fan-out for runs executing in the
    # worker process (no-op on SQLite or when event_bus_notify_enabled is off).
    start_event_listener()
    # Durable runs: pick up runs left pending/queued by a crash (or re-queued
    # by recover_stale_runs) so the inline backlog advances without a worker.
    # No-op in worker mode — the dedicated worker's poll owns claiming there.
    try:
        resumed = await resume_orphaned_runs()
        if resumed:
            logger.info("Resumed %s orphaned run(s) on boot", resumed)
    except Exception:
        logger.exception("Failed to resume orphaned runs on boot")
    # Re-dispatch background jobs stranded in queued by a restart — dispatch
    # only happens at create time otherwise, so without this they never run.
    try:
        from app.services.job_queue import dispatch_job
        from app.services.startup import pending_job_ids

        for job_id in pending_job_ids():
            asyncio.create_task(dispatch_job(job_id))
    except Exception:
        logger.exception("Failed to re-dispatch queued jobs on boot")
    # Do NOT start the in-process run worker here. In "worker" execution mode a
    # dedicated worker.py process owns run claiming/execution; starting the loop
    # here too would let both the API and the worker claim the same pending runs
    # (split-brain double-claim). In "inline" mode create_run schedules runs
    # directly, so no polling worker is needed either.
    # NOTE (single-process constraint): SSE streams and human-approval waits live
    # in the executor's in-memory broker/approval state. When runs execute in the
    # separate worker process, /stream and /approve served by the API process
    # cannot see that state. Cross-process streams/approvals require a shared
    # transport (out of scope for this fix).
    yield
    set_main_loop(None)
    await stop_run_worker()
    await stop_schedule_worker()
    await stop_event_listener()
    await shutdown_active_runs()
    await shutdown_http_client()
    shutdown_tracing()

async def rate_limit_middleware(request: Request, call_next):
    if rate_limited_path(request.url.path):
        try:
            check_rate_limit(request)
        except HTTPException as exc:
            # Raised inside middleware — translate directly; routing-level
            # exception handlers never see it (otherwise it falls through as
            # a 500 via the generic Exception handler).
            return JSONResponse(status_code=exc.status_code, content={"detail": exc.detail})
    return await call_next(request)


@app.middleware("http")
async def viewer_role_middleware(request: Request, call_next):
    """RBAC-lite: viewer keys are read-only across all mutating API methods."""
    if (
        settings.auth_enabled
        and request.url.path not in {"/v1/invoke", "/v1/invoke/"}
        and not request.url.path.startswith("/v1/chat/")
        and not (
            request.url.path.startswith("/v1/workflows/")
            and request.url.path.rstrip("/").endswith("/invoke")
        )
        and (
            request.url.path.startswith("/api/")
            or request.url.path.startswith("/v1/")
        )
        and request.method in {"POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE"}
    ):
        from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse as _JSONResponse

        from app.auth.deps import _resolve_api_token, role_from_api_key

        token = _resolve_api_token(
            request.headers.get("authorization"),
            request.headers.get("x-aegis-api-key"),
        )
        if role_from_api_key(token) == "viewer":
            return _JSONResponse(
                status_code=403, content={"detail": "Viewer keys are read-only"}
            )
    return await call_next(request)


def _health_db_counts() -> tuple[int, int]:
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        pending_runs = (
            db.query(models.WorkflowRun)
            .filter(models.WorkflowRun.status.in_(["pending", "queued"]))
            .count()
        )
        queued_jobs = (
            db.query(models.BackgroundJob)
            .filter(models.BackgroundJob.status == "queued")
            .count()
        )
        return pending_runs, queued_jobs
    finally:
        db.close()


@app.get("/health")
async def health(request: Request):
    db_ok = await asyncio.to_thread(check_database)
    startup_status = getattr(request.app.state, "startup_status", {})
    status = "ok" if db_ok else "degraded"

    pending_runs = 0
    queued_jobs = 0
    if db_ok:
        pending_runs, queued_jobs = await asyncio.to_thread(_health_db_counts)

    return {
        "status": status,
        "service": "aegis-backend",
        "version": "0.4.0",
        "auth_enabled": settings.auth_enabled,
        "database_ok": db_ok,
        "stale_runs_recovered": startup_status.get("stale_runs_recovered", 0),

+### Code node isolation
+
+Code nodes run CPython 3.13.15 for WASI inside [Wasmtime](https://bytecodealliance.github.io/wasmtime-py/), not the host Python interpreter. Each node gets a fresh VM in a short-lived subprocess with an empty environment, closed inherited descriptors, and no Python site hooks. A root service launches the native worker as `nobody` with no supplementary groups. Input and output cross the boundary as JSON, never pickle.
+
+The guest receives only its node input/context and the packaged Python standard library at `/lib` (read-only). Application files, databases, credentials, host environment variables, network sockets, shell commands, and native extensions are not available. Imports and interpreter attributes (`__*`, `gi_*`, `cr_*`, `ag_*`, `f_*`, `tb_*`, `co_*`, `mro`) remain blocked as defense in depth; the WASI capability boundary does not depend on that AST check.
+
+Limits: 4,000 source characters, 5 seconds wall time, 50 billion Wasmtime fuel units, 256 MiB guest linear memory, and 1 MiB combined guest stdout/stderr. The native child also has CPU/core/file-size rlimits on POSIX. The memory ceiling applies to the guest, not total native worker RSS. Timeouts kill and reap the child before releasing its concurrency slot.
+
+Provision once from `backend/` with `python -m app.services.code_runtime --fetch`. The provisioner verifies the pinned [CPython/WASI release](https://github.com/brettcannon/cpython-wasi-build/releases/tag/v3.13.15) SHA-256 before extraction and compilation. Docker builds and backend CI do this automatically; execution never downloads a runtime. Compiled artifacts are specific to the installed Wasmtime version, OS, and architecture. After upgrading Wasmtime, provision on each target again; restart after replacing an existing installation. Missing, incompatible, or changed essential runtime files fail closed—there is no native execution fallback. Keep Wasmtime patched and the managed runtime installation trusted.
+
 ---

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    from app.services.async_tasks import set_main_loop

    init_tracing()
    # NOTE: schema is owned by Alembic (single source of truth). We intentionally
    # do NOT call Base.metadata.create_all here — run_startup_tasks() instead
    # gates boot on migrations being current (see services/startup.py).
    startup_status = run_startup_tasks()
    app.state.startup_status = startup_status
    set_main_loop(asyncio.get_running_loop())
    await startup_http_client()
    start_schedule_worker()
    # Durable event transport: LISTEN/NOTIFY fan-out for runs executing in the
    # worker process (no-op on SQLite or when event_bus_notify_enabled is off).
    start_event_listener()
    # Durable runs: pick up runs left pending/queued by a crash (or re-queued
    # by recover_stale_runs) so the inline backlog advances without a worker.
    # No-op in worker mode — the dedicated worker's poll owns claiming there.
    try:
        resumed = await resume_orphaned_runs()
        if resumed:
            logger.info("Resumed %s orphaned run(s) on boot", resumed)
    except Exception:
        logger.exception("Failed to resume orphaned runs on boot")
    # Re-dispatch background jobs stranded in queued by a restart — dispatch
    # only happens at create time otherwise, so without this they never run.
    try:
        from app.services.job_queue import dispatch_job
        from app.services.startup import pending_job_ids

        for job_id in pending_job_ids():
            asyncio.create_task(dispatch_job(job_id))
    except Exception:
        logger.exception("Failed to re-dispatch queued jobs on boot")
    # Do NOT start the in-process run worker here. In "worker" execution mode a
    # dedicated worker.py process owns run claiming/execution; starting the loop
    # here too would let both the API and the worker claim the same pending runs
    # (split-brain double-claim). In "inline" mode create_run schedules runs
    # directly, so no polling worker is needed either.
    # NOTE (single-process constraint): SSE streams and human-approval waits live
    # in the executor's in-memory broker/approval state. When runs execute in the
    # separate worker process, /stream and /approve served by the API process
    # cannot see that state. Cross-process streams/approvals require a shared
    # transport (out of scope for this fix).
    yield
    set_main_loop(None)
    await stop_run_worker()
    await stop_schedule_worker()
    await stop_event_listener()
    await shutdown_active_runs()
    await shutdown_http_client()
    shutdown_tracing()

    return await call_next(request)


@app.middleware("http")
async def viewer_role_middleware(request: Request, call_next):
    """RBAC-lite: viewer keys are read-only across all mutating API methods."""
    if (
        settings.auth_enabled
        and request.url.path not in {"/v1/invoke", "/v1/invoke/"}
        and not request.url.path.startswith("/v1/chat/")
        and not (
            request.url.path.startswith("/v1/workflows/")
            and request.url.path.rstrip("/").endswith("/invoke")
        )
        and (
            request.url.path.startswith("/api/")
            or request.url.path.startswith("/v1/")
        )
        and request.method in {"POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE"}
    ):
        from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse as _JSONResponse

        from app.auth.deps import _resolve_api_token, role_from_api_key

        token = _resolve_api_token(
            request.headers.get("authorization"),
            request.headers.get("x-REDACTED-api-key"),
        )
        if role_from_api_key(token) == "viewer":
            return _JSONResponse(
                status_code=403, content={"detail": "Viewer keys are read-only"}
            )
    return await call_next(request)


def _health_db_counts() -> tuple[int, int]:
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        pending_runs = (
            db.query(models.WorkflowRun)
            .filter(models.WorkflowRun.status.in_(["pending", "queued"]))
            .count()
        )
        queued_jobs = (
            db.query(models.BackgroundJob)
            .filter(models.BackgroundJob.status == "queued")
            .count()
        )
        return pending_runs, queued_jobs
    finally:
        db.close()


@app.get("/health")
async def health(request: Request):
    db_ok = await asyncio.to_thread(check_database)
    startup_status = getattr(request.app.state, "startup_status", {})

    queued_jobs = 0

"""Standalone Aegis worker process for run execution and background jobs."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

import uvicorn
from fastapi import FastAPI

from app.config import settings
from app.logging_config import configure_logging
from app.services.run_worker import start_run_worker, stop_run_worker

configure_logging(settings.log_level)
logger = logging.getLogger("REDACTED.worker")


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_app: FastAPI):
    import asyncio

    from app.http_client import shutdown_http_client, startup_http_client
    from app.services.async_tasks import set_main_loop
    from app.services.executor import shutdown_active_runs
    from app.services.startup import check_migrations_current, recover_stale_runs
    from app.services.tracing import init_tracing, shutdown_tracing

    # Worker-mode runs execute in this process, so it must export their spans.
    init_tracing()
    # Schema is owned by Alembic (single source of truth) — same gate as the
    # API: refuse to boot when behind instead of create_all'ing a divergent
    # schema that wedges the database for both processes.
    check_migrations_current(
        strict=getattr(settings, "migration_check_strict", True)
    )
    # Worker owns recovery of runs left running/queued by a prior crash
    # (API process deliberately skips this when run_execution_mode=worker).
    # With resume_runs_on_boot this re-queues orphans for checkpoint resume
    # (which this worker's poll then claims); past resume_max_attempts it fails.
    recovered = recover_stale_runs(force=True)
    if recovered:
        logger.warning("Worker recovered %s stale run(s) on boot", recovered)
    set_main_loop(asyncio.get_running_loop())
    await startup_http_client()
    start_run_worker()
    logger.info("Worker process started", extra={"mode": settings.run_execution_mode})
    yield
    set_main_loop(None)
    await stop_run_worker()
    try:
        # stop_run_worker only stops the poller; runs it already scheduled are still
        # live. shutdown_active_runs cancels them and waits for the cancellation to
        # unwind, so their spans end before the provider closes — otherwise their
        # final spans are lost and later end() calls hit a closed provider.
        await shutdown_active_runs()
    finally:
        # Close (and flush) the provider even if draining raised.
        await shutdown_http_client()
        shutdown_tracing()


app = FastAPI(title="Aegis Worker", version="0.4.0", lifespan=lifespan)


@app.get("/health")
def health() -> dict[str, str]:
    return {"status": "ok", "service": "REDACTED-worker"}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("worker:app", host="0.0.0.0", port=int(getattr(settings, "worker_port", 8001) or 8001))
---

## Quick start

**Prerequisites:** Node 20+, Python 3.12+, and a [Google API key](https://ai.google.dev/) with Gemini access (the default provider — OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, and LiteLLM providers are optional per-node). Docker is only required when you choose the Postgres setup below; SQLite is the default for local development and tests.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/himanshu-nakrani/REDACTED.git
cd REDACTED
cp .env.example .env
# set GOOGLE_API_KEY (and DATABASE_URL if not using local Postgres)
```

**Database — choose one**

SQLite is the default in `.env.example`, so no database service is needed for a quick local run. To use it, leave `DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///./REDACTED.db` unchanged.

For Postgres, start the repository's pgvector image and set the connection string in `.env`:

```bash
docker compose up -d postgres
# DATABASE_URL=REDACTED
```

**Backend** — http://127.0.0.1:8000

```bash
cd backend
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m app.services.code_runtime --fetch
alembic upgrade head
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
```

For a separate run worker, use `RUN_EXECUTION_MODE=worker` in `.env`, then start the API and worker in separate terminals:

```bash
# Terminal 1 — from backend/
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000

# Terminal 2 — from backend/, with the same virtualenv and environment
python worker.py
```

Leave `RUN_EXECUTION_MODE=inline` (the default) when you want runs to execute in the API process.

**Frontend** — http://localhost:3000

```bash
cd frontend
cp .env.local.example .env.local   # NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:8000
npm install && npm run dev
```

**Health check**

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/health | jq .
# expect status: ok, database_ok: true
```

API docs: [http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs](http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs)

---

## Product surface

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Workflows  Templates  Observability  Guardrails  Prompts  Playground  Creds ... │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                                 │
│   Workspace health · Continue building · Needs attention                        │
│   Searchable workflow library       Pinned shortcuts                            │
│   Drafts │ In review │ Live          Recent activity                            │
│                                                                                 │
│   Canvas  ·  Inspector  ·  Run  ·  Versions  ·  Deploy / Chat                   │
│                                                                                 │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

| Area | What you get |
  Scheduler --> DB
  API --> Obs[Observability & traces]
  Obs --> DB
  Executor -.-> OTLP[OTLP / OpenTelemetry]
  Executor -.-> LangSmith[LangSmith OTLP export]
  Worker[Worker process worker.py] -.-> DB
  Worker -.-> Executor
```

Graphs live in Postgres. On run, the compiler validates the DAG and hands execution to **Google ADK 2.11**; each node's LLM provider resolves through `llm_providers` (Gemini natively, other providers via LiteLLM, or local keyless Ollama) while node events stream over SSE and quality signals update the ops surfaces.

| Layer | Stack |
|-------|--------|
| UI | Next.js 14 · React 18 · React Flow · TanStack Query · Tailwind · Lucide |
| API | FastAPI · SQLAlchemy 2 · Alembic · Pydantic Settings · Starlette |
| Runtime | Google ADK 2.11 · Gemini native + LiteLLM (OpenAI, Anthropic, Fireworks, OpenRouter, Featherless, Vercel AI Gateway) + local Ollama |
| Execution modes | `inline` (in API process) or `worker` (`worker.py` headless daemon via DB poll & `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` claiming) |
| Durability | Database checkpoints (`run_checkpoints`), restart recovery frontier re-wiring, database-backed `approval_requests` |
| Data & Vectors | PostgreSQL (SQLite for local/tests) · Vector retrieval: `auto` (pgvector on Postgres, sqlite-vec on SQLite, JSON fallback) |
| Telemetry | Structured logs · OpenTelemetry (OTLP) · LangSmith OTLP export with deep secret sanitization |
| Integrations | MCP client (stdio & Streamable HTTP) · Published workflow MCP server (`/mcp`) · Slack · Discord · Email · Postgres |

---

## Configuration

Minimal `.env`:

```bash
GOOGLE_API_KEY=your_google_api_key
DATABASE_URL=REDACTED
```

| Variable | Notes |
|----------|--------|
| `GOOGLE_API_KEY` | **Required** — Gemini (default provider) |
| `DATABASE_URL` | Postgres, or SQLite (`sqlite:///./REDACTED.db`, the default for local development and tests) |
| `GEMINI_MODEL` | Default `gemini-2.5-flash` |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` · `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` · `FIREWORKS_AI_API_KEY` · `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` · `FEATHERLESS_API_KEY` · `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` | Optional extra LLM providers — per-node selection; a bound credential overrides env |
| `OLLAMA_API_BASE` | Local or remote keyless Ollama base URL (default `http://localhost:11434`) |

"""Standalone Aegis worker process for run execution and background jobs."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

import uvicorn
from fastapi import FastAPI

from app.config import settings
from app.logging_config import configure_logging
from app.services.run_worker import start_run_worker, stop_run_worker

configure_logging(settings.log_level)
logger = logging.getLogger("REDACTED.worker")


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_app: FastAPI):
    import asyncio

    from app.http_client import shutdown_http_client, startup_http_client
    from app.services.async_tasks import set_main_loop
    from app.services.executor import shutdown_active_runs
    from app.services.startup import check_migrations_current, recover_stale_runs
    from app.services.tracing import init_tracing, shutdown_tracing

    # Worker-mode runs execute in this process, so it must export their spans.
    init_tracing()
    # Schema is owned by Alembic (single source of truth) — same gate as the
    # API: refuse to boot when behind instead of create_all'ing a divergent
    # schema that wedges the database for both processes.
    check_migrations_current(
        strict=getattr(settings, "migration_check_strict", True)
    )
    # Worker owns recovery of runs left running/queued by a prior crash
    # (API process deliberately skips this when run_execution_mode=worker).
    # With resume_runs_on_boot this re-queues orphans for checkpoint resume
    # (which this worker's poll then claims); past resume_max_attempts it fails.
    recovered = recover_stale_runs(force=True)
    if recovered:
        logger.warning("Worker recovered %s stale run(s) on boot", recovered)
    set_main_loop(asyncio.get_running_loop())
    await startup_http_client()
    start_run_worker()
    logger.info("Worker process started", extra={"mode": settings.run_execution_mode})
    yield
    set_main_loop(None)
    await stop_run_worker()
    try:
        # stop_run_worker only stops the poller; runs it already scheduled are still
        # live. shutdown_active_runs cancels them and waits for the cancellation to
        # unwind, so their spans end before the provider closes — otherwise their
        # final spans are lost and later end() calls hit a closed provider.
        await shutdown_active_runs()
    finally:
        # Close (and flush) the provider even if draining raised.
        await shutdown_http_client()
        shutdown_tracing()


app = FastAPI(title="Aegis Worker", version="0.4.0", lifespan=lifespan)


@app.get("/health")
def health() -> dict[str, str]:
    return {"status": "ok", "service": "REDACTED-worker"}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run("worker:app", host="0.0.0.0", port=int(getattr(settings, "worker_port", 8001) or 8001))

## Quick start

**Prerequisites:** Node 20+, Python 3.12+, and a [Google API key](https://ai.google.dev/) with Gemini access (the default provider — OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, and LiteLLM providers are optional per-node). Docker is only required when you choose the Postgres setup below; SQLite is the default for local development and tests.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/himanshu-nakrani/REDACTED.git
cd REDACTED
cp .env.example .env
# set GOOGLE_API_KEY (and DATABASE_URL if not using local Postgres)
```

**Database — choose one**

SQLite is the default in `.env.example`, so no database service is needed for a quick local run. To use it, leave `DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///./REDACTED.db` unchanged.

For Postgres, start the repository's pgvector image and set the connection string in `.env`:

```bash
docker compose up -d postgres
# DATABASE_URL=REDACTED
```

**Backend** — http://127.0.0.1:8000

```bash
cd backend
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m app.services.code_runtime --fetch
alembic upgrade head
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
```

For a separate run worker, use `RUN_EXECUTION_MODE=worker` in `.env`, then start the API and worker in separate terminals:

```bash
# Terminal 1 — from backend/
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000

# Terminal 2 — from backend/, with the same virtualenv and environment
python worker.py
```

Leave `RUN_EXECUTION_MODE=inline` (the default) when you want runs to execute in the API process.

**Frontend** — http://localhost:3000

```bash
cd frontend
cp .env.local.example .env.local   # NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:8000
npm install && npm run dev
```

**Health check**

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/health | jq .
# expect status: ok, database_ok: true
```

API docs: [http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs](http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs)
